Projects

Self-balancing robot

ESP32, MPU6050, L298N, C++

  • A two-wheeled robot that stays upright using live tilt data from an accelerometer and gyroscope.
  • A Kalman filter combines the sensor readings, and a PID controller adjusts motor speed to keep the robot balanced.
  • I built the hardware, wired the power and motor-driver electronics, and tuned the controller myself.
Code on GitHubWatch the demo

The pendulum at the top of this page is a small version of this project, rewritten to run in your browser. The original runs in CoppeliaSim.

Inverted pendulum PID simulation

CoppeliaSim

  • Simulated an inverted pendulum, an unstable system, and tuned a PID controller to stabilize it.
  • Studied how the Kp, Ki and Kd gains change oscillation, response and settling time across repeated runs.
  • I also taught this as a hands-on workshop (see below).

Meshmerize high-speed line follower

Arduino Nano, TB6612, TCRT5000, C++

  • Designed a custom 8-sensor infrared array and the full circuit for a fast line-following robot.
  • Wrote the sensor reading and steering code, using N20 500 RPM motors on a TB6612 driver with regulated power.
  • Placed 3rd at the Mumbai Zonals of Techfest 2026, IIT Bombay.

Autonomous maze solver

Arduino Uno, 3 x HC-SR04, C++

  • A robot that senses walls with three ultrasonic sensors and decides its route through a maze in real time.
  • Won 1st place at ALGORITHEM 2025, VIT Mumbai.

4-DOF robotic arm

ESP32, servo motors, CAD, 3D printing, C++

  • A four-joint arm driven by an ESP32, with coordinated motion across all joints.

Robotics Club Head

PID control workshop

I led a 1.5-hour hands-on session on PID theory: the P, I and D terms, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error. Participants tuned Kp, Ki and Kd to balance a pendulum in CoppeliaSim. I also walked through the electronics of a self-balancing robot, from battery to wheel.
